title: ECHO: Continuous Hierarchical Memory for Vision-Language-Action Models
claim: Tasks have natural hierarchical structure that flat linear storage ignores; embedding experiences in a hyperbolic tree space captures it and enables coarse-to-fine retrieval.
layout: 2 panels, left hierarchy diagram, right stacked flat-vs-ours comparison, dashed divider
description: The left panel, (a), shows a rounded box titled 'Hierarchical Semantic Structure of Manipulation'. Four robot photos run down the left edge. Beside them is a tree of colored bands: Macro (purple, 'Place banana in bowl'), Sub-task (blue, 'Pick up banana' and 'Place in bowl'), Action Primitives (green, e.g. 'Move to banana' and 'Close Gripper'), and Micro (gray, a row of empty control boxes). Black and red arrows run down the tree and mark one highlighted path. The right panel, (b), is split by a dashed line. The top half, 'Flat Linear Memory', shows a Query node fanning out to a row of yellow Memory 1…N boxes. The bottom half, 'Hyperbolic Hierarchical Memory (Ours)', shows a blue hyperbolic surface. Branches lead from it to green points inside overlapping colored regions, with a red retrieval path. An arrow on the left of this half runs from 'More abstract' to 'More specific'.
caption: Conceptual overview of the ECHO framework. (a) Manipulation demonstrations exhibit hierarchical semantics, where high-level task instructions are grounded through sub-tasks, action primitives, and micro-level controls. (b) Instead of organizing experiences as a flat linear memory, ECHO embeds them into a continuous hyperbolic hierarchical space, enabling coarse-to-fine memory organization, entailment-aware retrieval, and the generation of unseen memories through spatial interpolation.
abstract: Memory capacity is a critical factor determining the performance of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models in long-horizon manipulation tasks. Existing memory-augmented architectures primarily rely on linear or flat storage, lacking structural priors for manipulation categories and hierarchical organization. This deficiency hinders efficient experience retrieval and limits generalization to unseen long-horizon task compositions. Inspired by the hierarchical organization of human experience, we propose ECHO (Experience Consolidation and Hierarchical Organization), a novel memory framework operating within a Continuous Hierarchical Space. By employing a hyperbolic autoencoder, ECHO maps VLA hidden states into this space. Leveraging hyperbolic metrics and entailment constraint mechanisms, experience vectors are organized into a semantic memory tree that supports efficient top-down retrieval. In parallel, a background consolidation mechanism continuously refines the memory tree through geometric interpolation and structural splitting, supporting virtual memory synthesis in the continuous space. We integrate ECHO into the $Ï_0$ foundation model. Evaluations on LIBERO and preliminary real-world experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, notably achieving a 12.8% absolute improvement in execution success rate over the $Ï_0$ baseline on LIBERO-Long, while improving compositional generalization on cross-suite unseen long-horizon tasks.
